title.en: Growth and changing structure of employment

hook.en: A factory installs new machines and doubles its output, but hires only a handful of new workers. Is the economy growing?
hook.kn: ಒಂದು ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆ ಹೊಸ ಯಂತ್ರಗಳಿಂದ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ದುಪ್ಪಟ್ಟು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದರೆ ಕೆಲವೇ ಹೊಸ ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರನ್ನು ನೇಮಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಆರ್ಥಿಕತೆ ಬೆಳೆಯುತ್ತಿದೆಯೇ?

objectives.en: Classify activities into primary, secondary and tertiary sectors
Describe the changing structure of employment

narration.en: A factory installs new machines and doubles its output, but hires only a handful of new workers. Is the economy growing?
narration.kn: ಒಂದು ಕಾರ್ಖಾನೆ ಹೊಸ ಯಂತ್ರಗಳಿಂದ ಉತ್ಪಾದನೆ ದುಪ್ಪಟ್ಟು ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ, ಆದರೆ ಕೆಲವೇ ಹೊಸ ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರನ್ನು ನೇಮಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಆರ್ಥಿಕತೆ ಬೆಳೆಯುತ್ತಿದೆಯೇ?

body.en: Economic activities are grouped into three sectors. The primary sector includes agriculture, forestry, fishing, and mining and quarrying. The secondary sector includes manufacturing, construction, and electricity, gas and water supply. The tertiary or service sector includes trade, transport and storage, and services. In India the primary sector is still the largest employer, especially in rural areas, while in urban areas most workers are in the secondary and service sectors.

narration.en: The primary sector takes from nature, the secondary sector makes goods, and the tertiary sector provides services. In India the primary sector still employs the most workers, mainly in villages.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ವಲಯ ಪ್ರಕೃತಿಯಿಂದ ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ, ದ್ವಿತೀಯ ವಲಯ ಸರಕು ತಯಾರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ತೃತೀಯ ವಲಯ ಸೇವೆ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಭಾರತದಲ್ಲಿ ಇಂದಿಗೂ ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ವಲಯವೇ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಉದ್ಯೋಗ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.

narration.en: Let us see on the board how output and jobs can grow at different speeds.

say.en: Let us compare two growth paths over ten years, starting from an index of 100.
Suppose output, that is GDP, grows at 6 per cent a year. In ten years it reaches about 179.
Suppose jobs grow at only 2 per cent a year. Employment reaches just about 122.
The widening gap is jobless growth: more goods and services, but not enough new jobs.
Workers are also spread across three sectors. As an economy develops, labour should move from the first to the others.
Primary is farming, fishing and mining; secondary is manufacturing, construction and power; tertiary is trade, transport and services.
In India the primary sector still employs the largest share, especially in villages; services dominate in towns.

body.en: Between 1950 and 2010, India's GDP grew positively and faster than employment. When an economy produces more goods and services without a proportionate increase in employment opportunities, it is called jobless growth. As the economy developed, the share of workers in agriculture fell slowly and that of industry and services rose. At the same time a larger share of workers became casual wage labourers, a trend called casualisation of the workforce, which leaves workers more vulnerable.

points.en: GDP growth > employment growth = jobless growth
Slow shift of workers out of agriculture
Casualisation: rising share of casual work

narration.en: India's GDP grew faster than employment: that is jobless growth. Workers moved only slowly out of farming, and more of them became casual labourers, which we call casualisation.
narration.kn: ಭಾರತದ ಜಿಡಿಪಿ ಉದ್ಯೋಗಕ್ಕಿಂತ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಬೆಳೆಯಿತು: ಇದೇ ಉದ್ಯೋಗರಹಿತ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ. ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕಾರ್ಮಿಕರು ಅನಿಯತ ಕೂಲಿಗಳಾದರು; ಇದನ್ನು ಅನಿಯತೀಕರಣ ಎನ್ನುತ್ತೇವೆ.

caption.en: GDP index and employment index, both starting at 100. Change the two growth rates and watch the gap open up.

narration.en: Set the growth of GDP and of employment. When GDP grows much faster than jobs, we have jobless growth.

tryThis.en: Set g = 6 and n = 2. By how much does output per worker rise in 10 years?
Make n equal to g. Is there still jobless growth?
Why can output per worker rising be good news and bad news at the same time?

problem.en: A firm's output rises from ₹50 crore to ₹60 crore in a year, while its workforce rises from 1,000 to 1,020. Find the growth of output and of employment, and the change in output per worker.

steps.en: Output per worker: ₹50 crore ÷ 1,000 = ₹50 lakh; ₹60 crore ÷ 1,020 ≈ ₹58.8 lakh.
Output grew ten times as fast as jobs.

answer.en: Output +20%, jobs +2%, output per worker ₹50 lakh → about ₹58.8 lakh: jobless growth at the firm level.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A firm's output rises from ₹50 crore to ₹60 crore in a year, while its workforce rises from 1,000 to 1,020. Find the growth of output and of employment, and the change in output per worker.

body.en: Primary takes from nature, secondary makes in a factory, tertiary serves people. Mining comes from nature, so it is primary; electricity is produced, so it is secondary.

narration.en: Three sectors in three words: nature, factory, service.
Team quiz. Each team discusses and gives one answer.
narration.kn: ತಂಡ ರಸಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ. ಪ್ರತಿ ತಂಡ ಚರ್ಚಿಸಿ ಒಂದು ಉತ್ತರ ನೀಡಲಿ.

points.en: Primary: agriculture, fishing, mining; secondary: manufacturing, construction, power; tertiary: trade, transport, services.
points.kn: ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ: ಕೃಷಿ, ಮೀನುಗಾರಿಕೆ, ಗಣಿಗಾರಿಕೆ; ದ್ವಿತೀಯ: ತಯಾರಿಕೆ, ನಿರ್ಮಾಣ, ವಿದ್ಯುತ್; ತೃತೀಯ: ವ್ಯಾಪಾರ, ಸಾರಿಗೆ, ಸೇವೆಗಳು.

points.en: The primary sector is still India's largest employer.
points.kn: ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ವಲಯವೇ ಇಂದಿಗೂ ಭಾರತದ ಅತಿ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಉದ್ಯೋಗದಾತ.

points.en: GDP grew faster than employment: jobless growth; casual work rose: casualisation.
points.kn: ಜಿಡಿಪಿ ಉದ್ಯೋಗಕ್ಕಿಂತ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಬೆಳೆಯಿತು: ಉದ್ಯೋಗರಹಿತ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ; ಅನಿಯತ ಕೆಲಸ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿತು: ಅನಿಯತೀಕರಣ.

homework.en: Explain jobless growth with an example from your district.

narration.en: Recap. Primary: agriculture, fishing, mining; secondary: manufacturing, construction, power; tertiary: trade, transport, services. The primary sector is still India's largest employer. GDP grew faster than employment: jobless growth; casual work rose: casualisation.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ: ಕೃಷಿ, ಮೀನುಗಾರಿಕೆ, ಗಣಿಗಾರಿಕೆ; ದ್ವಿತೀಯ: ತಯಾರಿಕೆ, ನಿರ್ಮಾಣ, ವಿದ್ಯುತ್; ತೃತೀಯ: ವ್ಯಾಪಾರ, ಸಾರಿಗೆ, ಸೇವೆಗಳು. ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ವಲಯವೇ ಇಂದಿಗೂ ಭಾರತದ ಅತಿ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಉದ್ಯೋಗದಾತ. ಜಿಡಿಪಿ ಉದ್ಯೋಗಕ್ಕಿಂತ ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಬೆಳೆಯಿತು: ಉದ್ಯೋಗರಹಿತ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ; ಅನಿಯತ ಕೆಲಸ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿತು: ಅನಿಯತೀಕರಣ.
